prompt: What is the $y$-value of the horizontal asymptote of $f(x) = \frac{3x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 4}$?
hint: Compare the DEGREES of the top and bottom. Both are $2$ here.

hints.text: Compare the DEGREES of the top and bottom. Both are $2$ here.
When the degrees match, divide the leading coefficients: top $3$, bottom $1$.

explanation: Top degree $2$, bottom degree $2$ — a tie.
On a tie, the asymptote is the leading coefficient of the top over that of the bottom.

alternativeExplanations.title: Plug in a giant number
steps: Try $x = 1000$ and it is even closer to 3. The graph flattens out toward the line $y = 3$.
